card.name: Comparative word after a noun phrase
card.fires_on: The word 'more' (also 'greater', 'very', 'detail') placed right after a finished noun phrase, where it begins a comparison or adverb such as 'more frequently', 'more generally' or 'more than'.

modes.label: more frequently/generally
modes.description: 'more' follows a noun and leads into an adverb like frequently or generally.
modes.example: patients experienced more hostility- and aggression- related adverse reactions that were serious, severe, and led to dose reduction, interruption, and discontinuation<< more>> frequently than placebo-treated patients.

modes.label: more than a number
modes.description: 'more' after a noun introduces a quantity or time comparison.
modes.example: Interrupt treatment and closely monitor patients who develop aminotransferase elevations<< more>> than 3-times ULN

modes.label: detail or degree word
modes.description: Other degree words such as 'detail' or 'very' follow a noun phrase.
modes.example: Information in greater<< detail>> can be found at www.kidney

card.writes: It promotes words like 'timing' and 'opens' and suppresses adverb endings such as -ibly and -istically, so it favors what follows a comparison rather than an adverb ending.
card.plain: It fires on 'more' right after a noun, as in 'reactions more frequently than'.
